senses.definition: affected by an impairment of normal physical or mental function
examples: ill from the monotony of his suffering

senses.definition: distressing
indicating hostility or enmity
examples: you certainly did me an ill turn

senses.definition: presaging ill fortune
examples: my words with inauspicious thunderings shook heaven
a dead and ominous silence prevailed
a by-election at a time highly unpropitious for the Government

senses.definition: resulting in suffering or adversity
examples: it's an ill wind that blows no good

senses.definition: (‘ill’ is often used as a combining form) in a poor or improper or unsatisfactory manner; not well
examples: it ill befits a man to betray old friends
he performed badly on the exam

senses.definition: unfavorably or with disapproval
examples: tried not to speak ill of the dead
thought badly of him for his lack of concern

senses.definition: with difficulty or inconvenience; scarcely or hardly
examples: we can ill afford to buy a new car just now

senses.definition: an often persistent bodily disorder or disease; a cause for complaining
prohibited by law or by official or accepted rules
in an illegal manner
impairment of normal physiological function affecting part or all of an organism
add embellishments and paintings to (medieval manuscripts)
introduce light into
examples: This lamp lightens the room a bit

senses.definition: make free from confusion or ambiguity; make clear
examples: Clear up the question of who is at fault

senses.definition: clarify by giving an example of
depict with an illustration
supply with illustrations
a visual representation (a picture or diagram) that is used to make some subject more pleasing or easier to understand
an item of information that is typical of a class or group
examples: this patient provides a typical example of the syndrome
there is an example on page 10

senses.definition: artwork that helps make something clear or attractive
showing by example
